# Detailed Summary — Unit 6: Animal Tissue
### Persona: Beginner | D_target: 2 | Images: 20

---

## H1. History of Animal Histology

The study of animal tissue was revolutionized by **Marie Francois Xavier Bichat (1771–1802)**, a French anatomist and pathologist. He is credited with:
- Coining the term **'tissue'** in terms of animal anatomy.
- Being recognized as **'Founder of Animal Histology'** — for proposing that tissues are the central element in anatomy.
- Being recognized as **'Father of Histology'** — for distinguishing **21 types of elementary tissues** from which organs of the human body are made.
- Achieving all this **without a microscope**.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Phylum Coelenterata: first animal tissue, tissue-grade organization" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

> 📌 **Quick Memory Aid**: Bichat = coined "tissue" + 21 types + no microscope + Father AND Founder of animal histology.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Overview: all major histologists and tissue-grade hierarchy timeline" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

Two other important scientists:
- **Karl Mayer (1801)**: Coined the term **'histology'**.
- **Marcello Malpighi (1628–1694)**: Recognized as the **Founder of Histology**.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Xavier Bichat portrait and contributions: coined 'tissue', 21 types, no microscope" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

### What is Animal Tissue?

Animal tissue is a **group of cells** having a common **origin**, but whose **structure**, **location**, and **function** may be similar or dissimilar.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Chapter overview: four types of animal tissue and their roles" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

- **Cells** group together → **Tissues**
- **Tissues** group together → **Organs**
- **Organs** group together → **Organ-systems**
- **Organ-systems** form → **Organisms**

### Histo-Components of Animal Tissue

Cells of animal tissue may or may not secrete **matrix**:
- **Connective tissue** → 3 histo-components: Cells + Matrix + Fibres
- **Epithelial, Muscular, Nervous tissue** → 2 histo-components: Cells + Matrix only

### Four Types of Animal Tissue

Animal tissues are classified into **four types** based on origin, structure, location, and function:

```mermaid
mindmap
  root((Animal Tissue))
    Epithelial
      Covering and lining
      Secreting
    Connective
      Binds
      Supports
      Circulates
    Muscular
      Voluntary
      Involuntary
    Nervous
      Controls
      Regulates
```

> 💡 **Do you know?** Animal tissue was first seen in **Phylum Coelenterata** (tissue-grade organization). All 4 types were first seen together in **Phylum Platyhelminthes**.

---

## H2. Epithelial Tissue — The Covering Tissue

Epithelial tissue, also called **epithelium**, is the **covering, lining, forming, and secreting tissue** of animals. It:
- **Covers** body surfaces, organs, and tissues.
- **Lines** coelomic (body) cavities.
- **Forms** glands and blood vessels.
- **Secretes** enzymes and hormones.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="General features of epithelial tissue: all key properties combined" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

### Key Properties at a Glance

| Feature | Epithelial Tissue |
|---------|-------------------|
| Cell count | Most numerous (maximum cells) |
| Matrix | Minimal (no fibres) |
| Blood supply | **Avascular** (no blood vessels) |
| Nutrition method | **Diffusion** |
| Basement membrane | Present (made of **white collagen**) |
| Origin | All 3 germ layers (Ecto + Meso + Endoderm) |

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Epithelial tissue types overview infographic" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

> 🔬 **Skin coverage**: Epithelium covers the **largest surface area** — 1.6–1.8 m² in adult humans.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Four types of cell junctions in epithelial tissue" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

Cells are held together by **4 cell junctions**:
1. **Tight junction** (Zonula occludens)
2. **Adherens junction** (Zonula adherens)
3. **Desmosome** (Macula adherens)
4. **Gap junction** (Septate junction)

### Surfaces by Coelom Type

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Acoelomate e.g. Flatworm] --> B[2 surfaces: 1 covering + 1 lining]
  C[Pseudocoelomate e.g. Roundworm] --> D[3 surfaces: 1 covering + 2 linings]
  E[Coelomate e.g. Earthworm] --> F[4 surfaces: 2 covering + 2 linings]
```

### Types of Epithelial Tissue — Overview

Epithelial tissues are classified by **number of cell layers**:

1. **Simple Epithelium** → 1 cell layer
2. **Compound Epithelium** → Multiple cell layers

---

### 2.1 Simple EpitheliumSimple epithelium has a **single layer of cells** all resting on a basement membrane. The four types are:

#### I. Simple Squamous Epithelium- Cells are **thin, flattened, and polygonal** with flat, oval nucleus.
- Also called **tessellated**, **pavement**, or **mosaic epithelium**.

**Key Locations:**
- **Alveoli of lungs** — gaseous exchange
- **Bowman's capsule** — ultrafiltration
- **Coelom** — lining the body cavity
- **Capillary** — formation of capillary + blood circulation
- **Descending limb of loop of Henle** — selective reabsorption

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Guide to all simple epithelial tissue types" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

> 💡 **Endothelium vs Mesothelium**:
> - **Endothelium** = simple squamous from **endoderm** → capillary, endocardium, tunica interna.
> - **Mesothelium** = simple squamous from **mesoderm** → parietal epithelium, visceral/splanchnic epithelium, mesenteries.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Simple squamous: endothelium vs mesothelium comparison" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

#### II. Simple Cuboidal Epithelium

- Cells are **moderate-sized, polyhedral** with equal height and width; large, spherical, central nucleus.
- Types: Non-ciliated, Ciliated, Brush-bordered (microvilli).
- **Brush-bordered cuboidal** in **PCT of nephrons** for selective reabsorption.

#### III. Simple Columnar Epithelium

- Cells are **tall, cylindrical** with height > width; elongated oval nucleus at basal region.
- **Non-ciliated columnar** in gall bladder (bile storage), stomach + intestine (secretion, absorption, excretion).
- **Ciliated columnar** in fallopian tube (capture ovum) and neurocoel (circulate CSF).
- **Brush-bordered columnar** in **intestinal mucosa** for absorption.

#### IV. Pseudostratified Epithelium

- **Appears multi-layered** but is actually a **single layer** of cuboidal + columnar cells, all touching the basement membrane.
- Columnar cells modified into: **Goblet cells** (secrete mucous) + **Ciliated cells** (filter air).
- Located in **upper respiratory tract, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles** — filters dust from air.

---

### 2.2 Compound Epithelium

Compound epithelium has **many layers of cells**. Types:

#### I. Stratified Epithelium (no stress)

- **Stratified Squamous — Non-keratinized**: Smooth surface; in buccal cavity, oesophagus, vagina — keeps surface moist.
- **Stratified Squamous — Keratinized**: Rough surface (keratin secreted); in **skin + derivatives** — waterproof, protection.

> 💡 **Keratin** = scleroprotein, secreted only by vertebrates. Found on: Fish (scales), Reptiles (dry scales, claws), Birds (feathers, beak, claws), Mammals (hair, horn, hoof, nails, claws).

- **Stratified Cuboidal**: Rare-type — in ducts of salivary, sweat, and mammary glands.
- **Stratified Columnar**: Uncommon-type — in conjunctiva, pharynx, male urethra.

#### II. Transitional Epithelium (bears stress)

- Also called **Urothelium** or **Plastic epithelium**.
- Cells **change shape**: rounded (relaxed) → flattened/squamous (when stretched).
- Located in: **Renal pelvis, Ureter, Urinary bladder, Urethra** — permits high expansion.

---

### 2.3 Modified Epithelium (Beginner overview)Six types of modification on the free border of epithelial cells:

1. **Ciliated** — Kino-ciliated (9+2 arrangement, e.g., respiratory); Stereo-ciliated (0+0, in epididymis).
2. **Brush-bordered** — Microvilli for absorption (kidney tubules, small intestine).
3. **Neuro-sensory** — Sensory hairs connected to nerve fibres (olfactory epithelium — smelling).
4. **Pigmented** — Pigment-containing cells (retina).
5. **Germinal** — Gamete-forming cells (testes + ovaries).
6. **Glandular** — Glands secreting enzymes or hormones (3 main categories by duct presence: Exocrine, Endocrine, Heterocrine).

## H3. Connective Tissue — The Binding, Supporting, and Circulating Tissue

Connective tissue is the **most abundant animal tissue** and the only tissue to have **three histo-components**: cells, matrix, and fibres.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Proper connective tissue infographic" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

| Feature | Connective Tissue |
|---------|-------------------|
| Origin | Mesoderm |
| Cells | Fewer (least) |
| Matrix | Most abundant |
| Fibres | Abundant |

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Connective Tissue overview: binding, supporting, circulating" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

### Functions
- **Binds**: similar-to-similar AND dissimilar-to-dissimilar tissues.
- **Supports**: forms structural framework of organs and whole animals.
- **Circulates**: transports materials from place to place.

> ⚠️ Important: Connective tissue NEVER binds nervous tissue. Neurones are bound by **neuroglia** (their own supportive cells).

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="CT Structure overview: cells, matrix, fibres relationship" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

### Three Types of Connective Tissue

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Connective Tissue]
  A --> B[1. Proper CT\nBinds]
  A --> C[2. Supportive CT\nSupports]
  A --> D[3. Fluid CT\nCirculates]
  B --> B1[Loose-matrix\nAreolar + Adipose]
  B --> B2[Dense-matrix\nWhite fibrous + Tendon + Ligament]
  C --> C1[Cartilage\n4 types]
  C --> C2[Bone\nVascular]
  D --> D1[Blood]
  D --> D2[Lymph]
```

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Supportive CT: Cartilage and Bone comparison" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

---

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Fluid connective tissue: Blood and Lymph overview" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

### 3.1 Proper Connective Tissue

**Cells** (5 types):
- **Fibroblasts**: Principal cells; elongated, irregular shape; secrete matrix and fibres.
- **Mast cells**: Modified basophils; oval; secrete heparin (anticoagulant), histamine (allergy/inflammation/vasodilation), serotonin (vasoconstriction). **Found only in proper CT.**
- **Histocytes**: Modified monocytes; amoeboid macrophages; engulf foreign particles, dead cells, microbes. **Found only in proper CT.**
- **Lymphocytes**: Type of WBC; also in proper CT; secrete antibodies.
- **Plasma cells**: Cartwheel cells; modified lymphocytes; secrete immunoglobulins against antigens.

**Fibres** (3 types):

| Fibre | Protein | Colour | Properties |
|-------|---------|--------|------------|
| Collagen | Collagen | **White** | Thick, wavy, unbranched, inelastic, in bundles |
| Elastic | Elastin | **Yellow** | Thin, branched, elastic, no bundle |
| Reticulate | Reticulin | **Colourless** | Ultrathin, network-forming, form **stroma** |

> 💡 When collagen fibres are boiled in water → converted into **gelatin**.

**Loose-Matrix Proper CT:**
- **Areolar tissue**: Soft, packing tissue; between skin and muscles; between sub-mucosa and muscularis mucosa.
- **Adipose tissue**: Modified areolar + adipocytes (fat cells). White adipocytes (white/yellow fat — abdomen, hump, blubber); Brown adipocytes (brown fat — migratory birds, hibernating rats, newborns).

**Dense-Matrix Proper CT:**
- **Tendon**: Connects **muscle to bone** (thin collagen bundles).
- **Ligament**: Connects **bone to bone** (thick collagen + some elastic fibres).
- **White fibrous tissue**: Covers skull sutures (immovable), sclerotic of mammalian eye, periosteum and perichondrium.

---

### 3.2 Supportive Connective Tissue**Cartilage** — avascular, flexible supportive CT:
- Cells: Chondroblasts (immature) + Chondrocytes (mature) in lacunae.
- Matrix: Semisolid **chondrin** (muco-protein).
- Covered by **perichondrium** (except at articular surface).
- 4 types: Hyaline (transparent, most abundant), Calcified (coated CaCO₃), Fibrocartilage (strongest, no perichondrium), Elastic (yellow fibres, pinna, larynx).

**Bone** — vascular, rigid supportive CT:
- Cells: Osteoblasts (immature) + Osteocytes (mature) in lacunae with canaliculi.
- Matrix: Solid **ossein** (muco-protein); 65% inorganic (Ca₃PO₄ = 95%) + 15% organic + 10% water.
- Covered by **periosteum** (except articular surface).
- Long bone: **Epiphysis** (red marrow, haemopoiesis, spongy, no Haversian system) + **Diaphysis** (yellow marrow, fat storage, Haversian system, compact bone).

> 💡 **Haversian system** is diagnostic of **mammalian bone** only.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Blood anatomy and chemistry: plasma + corpuscles" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

---

### 3.3 Fluid Connective Tissue

**Blood** (8% of human body weight):
- **Plasma** (55%): 90% water + 7% proteins (Albumins — osmotic pressure; Globulins — transport + immunity) + 3% others.
- **Blood cells** (45%): RBCs + WBCs + Platelets.

| Component | Details |
|-----------|---------|
| RBCs | Biconcave (mammal); non-nucleated; haemoglobin; O₂ + CO₂ transport; 120 days lifespan |
| WBCs | RBC:WBC = 600:1; 4500–10000 mm⁻³; 12–20 days; phagocytic + antibody-forming |
| Platelets | 0.15–0.4 million mm⁻³; 7–10 days; thromboplastin release for clotting |

---

## H4. Muscular Tissue — The Contractile TissueMuscular tissue is **contractile tissue**; mesodermal in origin. It performs **locomotion and movement** through contraction and relaxation.

| Type | Shape | Nucleus | Voluntary? | Fatigues? |
|------|-------|---------|------------|-----------|
| Skeletal/Striped | Cylindrical, unbranched | Many (syncytial) | **Yes** | **Immediately** |
| Smooth/Unstriped | Spindle, tapering | Single | **No** | After ~10–12 hrs |
| Cardiac | Cylindrical, branched | Single | **No** | **Never** |

- **Sarcomere**: Basic contractile unit; Z-lines on either side; dark band = **myosin** (A-band); light band = **actin** (I-band).
- **Muscle coverings**: Endomysium (myofibre) → Perimysium (fascicle) → Epimysium (block).
- **Cardiac muscle**: has **intercalated discs** between cardiocytes; faint striations.
- **Sliding filament theory** of muscle contraction: proposed by **Huxley and Hanson**.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Includes muscular tissue overview" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

---

## H5. Nervous Tissue — The Control Tissue

Nervous tissue **controls, coordinates, integrates, and regulates** organisms; **ectodermal** in origin.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Nervous Tissue]
  A --> B[Neuroglia\nSupport cells\nCAN do mitosis]
  A --> C[Neurones\nStructural + Functional unit\nCANNOT do mitosis]
  B --> B1[CNS: Astrocyte, Oligodendrocyte, Microglia, Ependymal]
  B --> B2[PNS: Stellate, Schwann cell]
  C --> C1[Soma / Cyton]
  C --> C2[Neurites: Dendrite + Axon]
```

### Neuroglia
- **Astrocyte**: Star-shaped; regulates neuro-environment; heals brain injury.
- **Oligodendrocyte**: Forms **myelin sheath** in CNS.
- **Microglia**: Macrophages; **mesodermal** origin (exception — rest are ectodermal).
- **Ependymal cell**: Lines ventricles; secretes **CSF**.
- **Schwann cell** (PNS): Forms myelin sheath in PNS; heals injury.

### Neurone Structure

- **Soma (Cyton/Cell body)**: Star-shaped; contains **Nissl's granules** (RNA + ribosomes + RER); gray.
- **Dendrite**: Short, branched; carries impulse **into** soma → **afferent/sensory**.
- **Axon (Nerve fibre)**: Single, unbranched, longest; carries impulse **out of** soma → **efferent/motor**.

### Myelinated vs Non-Myelinated

| Feature | Myelinated | Non-Myelinated |
|---------|------------|----------------|
| Colour | White | Gray |
| Speed | **Fast** (saltatory conduction) | Slow |
| Node of Ranvier | **Present** | Absent |
| Location | White matter | Gray matter |

- **Gray matter**: Outer brain + Inner spinal cord.
- **White matter**: Inner brain + Outer spinal cord.
